title: Alibaba's Joe Tsai Says Open Source Is Europe's Best Shot at AI
source_used: Bloomberg text read on The Edge Malaysia copy (bloomberg.com returned 403)
key_facts: Alibaba Group chairman Joe Tsai said open-source AI is Europe's best route to technological independence from the US and China.
He spoke at the Wave by Vento conference in Turin, Italy, on Wednesday, 7 Oct 2026.
He urged Europe to build compute infrastructure to train models and run inference on Europe-based infrastructure.
He said Europe should train models on proprietary industrial data, citing China's factory data as an example.
He said he is bullish on Europe's neoclouds, specialised cloud firms running data centres with AI chips.
He said US closed-source labs do not publish papers any more and 'want to be closed'.
quote_evidence: "No country would want to entirely trust another country’s technology: if there’s a change in government, a change in circumstances, they can just shut off the technology from you," he said, speaking at the Wave by Vento conference in Turin, Italy, on Wednesday.

"What Europe needs to do is to get really serious about creating the compute infrastructure to allow these models to run, to train the models and run inference on Europe-based infrastructure," he continued, referring to the process of running AI systems after they’ve been trained.
why_it_matters_hint: A major Asian tech chairman sets out a sovereignty route for Europe's AI that depends on its own compute.
notes: Event on 7 Oct, so NEW; score kept at 6. Read on The Edge Malaysia copy of the Bloomberg text; Bloomberg is the source. The quote 'They want to be closed' is short and attributed.
